title: Resort Lodging Terms: Free Cancellation Periods and Nights Retained
content:
These are the figures that stand behind the cancellation terms of a Resort Lodging reservation. Each unit type publishes a free cancellation period, being the number of calendar days before arrival up to which a cancellation carries no fee; a number of late cancellation nights, being the nights of the room rate retained when a cancellation is recorded after the free cancellation deadline; and a number of unclaimed nights, being the nights of the room rate retained when the party never arrives.

| Unit type | Free cancellation period (calendar days before arrival) | Late cancellation nights retained | Unclaimed nights retained |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base Village Inn Room | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| Slopeside Studio | 7 | 1 | 2 |
| Slopeside One-Bedroom Residence | 14 | 2 | 2 |
| Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence | 14 | 2 | 3 |
| Mountain Lodge Suite | 21 | 2 | 3 |
| Summit Penthouse Residence | 30 | 3 | 4 |
| Private Mountain Chalet | 45 | 5 | 7 |

### How the three figures differ

The free cancellation period is a length of notice measured in calendar days; the other two are counts of nights of the room rate, and they are not the same figure as each other. For the Slopeside Studio the late cancellation nights number 1 while the unclaimed nights number 2; for the Base Village Inn Room both number 1. The largest unit types carry both the longest notice and the heaviest counts: the Private Mountain Chalet publishes 45 calendar days of free cancellation, 5 late cancellation nights and 7 unclaimed nights.
